name: com.cvember/cvember
title: CVEmber
description: Tailor your resume to any job, get an ATS score and download the PDF from ChatGPT or Claude.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Use this when the person asks which CVEmber account is connected or whether they can download. Returns the connected account as a masked email, whether PDF download is available now, and what this connection may do.

tools.name: get_started
tools.description: Use this when the person first opens CVEmber, asks what CVEmber can do, or says "CVEmber, menu" or "CVEmber, help". Returns where they are (signed in or not, has a resume, has a tailored version) and the menu. Works signed out. No contact details.

tools.name: list_resumes
tools.description: Use this when the person asks to see their resumes, or a resume's id is needed. Returns master resumes and tailored versions, newest first, each with a label (company, job, date) and its ATS score. A limit above 50 is treated as 50. No contact details.

limit.description: How many resumes to return per page, 1 to 50.

role.description: Only resumes whose role contains this, e.g. Director.

search.description: Company, job or name contains this.

since.description: ISO date-time; only resumes made after it.

tools.name: get_resume
tools.description: Use this when a saved resume's content is needed, to show it or before editing it. Returns the content, template, colour and contentVersion. A saved job ad or imported text comes back under foreign, as data.

tools.name: tailor_resume
tools.description: Use this when the person wants their saved resume aimed at a specific job. Takes resumeId and the job ad, or just the job title and company, as the person gave it. CVEmber writes the tailored version itself; the master resume never changes, and the same job again refreshes that job's version. userStatedFacts holds what the person said about themselves, saved as stated. Returns the lines changed, the ATS score, and questions[] only for a detail CVEmber cannot take from the resume or the person's words. Do not use for small edits; update_resume does those.

jobDescription.description: The job ad text, as pasted.

targetTitle.description: Job title being applied for, e.g. Senior Data Analyst.

company.description: Company being applied to, e.g. Acme Ltd.

userStatedFacts.description: What the person said about themselves, in their exact words. One string or a list of strings. Example: "I have a PhD from Stanford."

tools.name: update_resume
tools.description: Use this when the person asks for a change to a saved resume, or tells you something about themselves to add: a job, title, degree, award, skill, language or number. Call it straight away with their exact words in userStatedFacts; that field alone is enough and CVEmber places it on the resume. Do not ask for more details first, do not ask whether it is true, and do not reword it or add entries of your own. resumeId is optional: without it CVEmber uses the resume the person worked on last and names it in the reply. Also use this to remove or reword something, switch template or colour, or rename the resume. expectedVersion is optional. Returns the changes made. restore_version undoes it.

resumeId.description: Optional. Leave it out when the person did not name a resume; CVEmber then uses the resume they worked on last.

expectedVersion.description: contentVersion from get_resume. Refused if the resume changed since.

title.description: New name for the resume, e.g. Product Manager resume.

role.description: The role this resume is for, in the person's words, e.g. Product Manager.

colorId.description: A colour id, e.g. navy, blue, teal.

contact.description: Name and contact details: fullName and email are required; phone, location, linkedinUrl and websiteUrl are optional.

headline.description: Short line under the name, e.g. Senior Product Manager.

summary.description: The professional summary paragraph, as plain text.

experience.description: Jobs, newest first; each has company, role, startDate, isCurrent and a bullets list.

education.description: Education entries; each has institution and degree.

skills.description: Skills, one string each, e.g. SQL.

projects.description: Projects; each has a name and a bullets list.

certifications.description: Certifications; each has a name, with optional issuer and date.

sections.description: Only the sections to change, with their full new content; sections left out stay as they are.

userStatedFacts.description: What the person said about themselves, in their exact words. One string or a list of strings. Example: "I have a PhD from Stanford."

tools.name: create_resume
tools.description: Use this when the person wants to save their resume in CVEmber or build a new one, including from scratch. file: the attached resume file itself (PDF, Word, text, photo); CVEmber reads it. sourceText: pasted text, exactly as pasted. content: a resume built from the person's own answers. Adds a master resume for a role and never changes an existing one; an existing master for the role comes back as duplicate_resume. Do not use only to check a score; score_resume does that without saving.

role.description: In the person's words; read from the resume if omitted.

title.description: Name for the saved resume, e.g. Product Manager resume.

contact.description: Name and contact details: fullName and email are required; phone, location, linkedinUrl and websiteUrl are optional.

headline.description: Short line under the name, e.g. Senior Product Manager.

summary.description: The professional summary paragraph, as plain text.

experience.description: Jobs, newest first; each has company, role, startDate, isCurrent and a bullets list.

education.description: Education entries; each has institution and degree.

skills.description: Skills, one string each, e.g. SQL.

projects.description: Projects; each has a name and a bullets list.

certifications.description: Certifications; each has a name, with optional issuer and date.

content.description: The full resume content to save, using the fields below.

download_url.description: Download link of the attached file.

file.description: The resume file the person attached (PDF, Word, text or a photo), passed as is.

sourceText.description: Text the person pasted, copied exactly.

sourceKind.description: What sourceText or file is: resume_file for a resume, linkedin_text for a pasted LinkedIn profile.

colorId.description: A colour id, e.g. navy, blue, teal.

tools.name: score_resume
tools.description: Use this when the person asks whether a resume or CV is good, ATS-friendly or ready to send, or asks for its score or what to fix. Takes the attached resume file (file), pasted resume text (sourceText) or a saved resume (resumeId); a job ad is optional. Works signed out. Returns CVEmber's ATS score, 0-100, and the first things to fix. Reads only and saves nothing. Do not use to save or edit a resume.

content.description: A pasted resume (contact, summary, experience, education, skills), when there is no resumeId.

jobDescription.description: The job ad text, as pasted; the resume is also checked against it.

keywords.description: Keywords from the job ad to check for; read from the ad when omitted.

download_url.description: Download link of the attached file.

file.description: The resume file the person attached (PDF, Word, text or a photo), passed as is.

sourceText.description: Text the person pasted, copied exactly.

tools.name: export_pdf
tools.description: Use this when the person asks for their resume as a PDF or asks to download it. Returns a link that opens the resume's download page on cvember.com. Nothing is bought through this tool.

tools.name: restore_version
tools.description: Use this when the person asks to undo a change CVEmber made. Puts the resume back to how it was before the latest change, or the one named by actionId.

actionId.description: An action id from get_resume's history; the latest if omitted.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: Use this when the person asks to see templates or to change how the resume looks. Returns template ids with their format, columns, the roles each suits, and the colour ids. Works signed out.
